summary: Independently verified the ADR-028 clause 2 authoritative restart-required set against the working tree (base 8b29dfa). The classification is complete and correct for all 43 current user-adjustable settings: I checked every restart-required entry and its named construction-capture site against the actual code, checked all 36 per-operation entries for missed construction captures, and confirmed no singleton captures a currently per-operation setting. The seven-setting set (mixed: SourceArtifactLimitBytes, DerivedArtifactLimitBytes, MaxImageDimensionPixels; restart-only: RenderCacheTtlMinutes, RenderCacheQuotaBytes, ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes, TerminalProvenanceRetentionDays) is accurate; the inert global OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds finding is confirmed and its per-operation-with-note classification is defensible under the binary ADR rule and correctly disclosed. The scope is clean and the docs/state/changelog are accurate except for one claim about test coverage. The single required change: the 'no-silent-member' guard does not actually cover PluginConfiguration (its five properties are hardcoded rather than reflected), so a future PluginConfiguration leaf property can be silently left unclassified, contrary to the worker report and changelog claim of 'reflection over the five configuration model types with container recursion'. findings.summary: The no-silent-member classification guard does not cover PluginConfiguration, and the worker report/changelog overstate it as reflection over all five configuration model types.
findings.detail: RestartRequiredSettingsTests.EveryUserAdjustableConfigurationPropertyIsClassified builds its expected domain via ExpectedClassifiedNames(). That helper adds PluginConfiguration's five properties by hand (RestartRequiredSettingsTests.cs 287-291: LogVerbosity, WebhookSecret, EnabledLibraries, BadgeMoviePosters, BadgeEpisodePosters) and only reflects over ArrConnectionConfiguration, OperationalLimits, RendererConfiguration, and BadgeSelectorConfiguration (lines 293-318). There is no container recursion anywhere. Consequence: if a new writable leaf property is added to PluginConfiguration and not classified, it is absent from both RestartRequiredSettings.All and the hardcoded expected set, so neither 'missing' nor 'unknown' is non-empty and the test still passes. The worker report (summary line 10; acceptance_criteria line 57; test_sensitivity line 109), the changelog entry ('no-silent-member reflection over the five configuration model types'), and the consumer-evidence doc all claim the opposite. I verified the omission is not necessary: BasePluginConfiguration (the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 base type) exposes no public properties or fields, so reflecting over PluginConfiguration with the existing WritableLeafProperties/IsClassifiedLeaf filter yields exactly the same five properties that are currently hardcoded. The other four types are genuinely guarded.

findings.summary: Classifying the inert global OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds as per-operation-with-note is defensible under the binary rule and is disclosed, not silently omitted.
findings.detail: Exhaustive grep of src/ArrTags confirms OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds is read only by Validate (range check), Clone, the XML serializer, and the settings page; no runtime consumer exists. The effective timeout is ArrConnectionConfiguration.RequestTimeoutSeconds, applied per client creation by ArrHttpClientFactory (50). ADR-028 clause 2 defines restart-required as 'any consumer resolves the value at singleton construction' and per-operation as 'every consumer resolves it from the current snapshot per operation'; with zero consumers the universal is vacuously satisfied, so per-operation is the rule-consistent classification, and marking it restart-required would be a false page claim (a restart would not apply it either). The worker records this in SettingClassification.Note, in consumer-evidence.md section 5, and in known_limitations, and a test pins it as the only classified setting without a runtime consumer. No functional defect. Recommended (non-blocking) follow-up: record the inert field explicitly in the canonical limitations register or orchestrator state so a future task can remove/repurpose it; it is currently tracked only in this task's report/evidence.
